- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for bearish momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect; cap forecast decline to avoid excessive overshoot.  
- If recent sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model should not forecast upward moves beyond 1–2 days.  
- If forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), apply downward bias proportional to sentiment magnitude.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows mean reversion toward 60–65, model should not forecast above 65 unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is flat or declining, adjust upward by 3–5% to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.  
- Avoid forecasting below 60 when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — model tends to underestimate support.
